label: Claude Haiku 5.5
output:
To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Handover: launch Thursday 26 November (draft)

DRAFT, for Marieke to read before sharing

Inês,

I'm sorry to leave you with this. My father is ill and I am with my family, and I'm taking the train tonight. I don't know yet how long I'll be away. I should have found the figure 3 error earlier, so the mess is mine, not yours. I trust you completely with this launch. You ran the annex B sensitivity runs yourself, you know the paper as well as I do, and in Lisbon you rescued my panel when the projector died. You are better live than you think.

Below is what needs doing and in what order. Everything is in this folder and in my inbox.

1. The number that changes: 2.1 becomes 1.4

The 2030 LDC-relevant revenue estimate is EUR 1.4 billion. The 2.1 figure came from the old run, before the free allocation phase-out was applied. PDF v7 on the drive is corrected (pages 3, 14 and 15), and so is figure 3. The conclusion of the paper does not change, only the headline number. Use v7 for everything from now on, and make sure nobody sends or prints an older PDF.

2. Tuesday 24 November

Check deck v4. Slides 6 and 9 still show 2.1, and slide 9 has the revenue chart. Change both to 1.4 and check the speaker notes for the old figure. The 14-slide version is good, by the way. I wish I could go through it with you.

Also, Tomás from the MEP's office asked for changes to the timing (see section 4). I haven't replied yet.

3. Wednesday 25 November

Badges: Tomás needs the final names of everyone from our side by 12:00 at the latest, or security will not let them in. Please send him the list before then.

Press release: the release went to our 34 Brussels contacts on Friday afternoon under embargo, and it says 2.1. It has to be corrected. First thing, speak to Hanna and ask her to send a correction to the same 34 contacts with 1.4, before the press calls. If she needs a senior name on it, Geert can sign off. He knows I'm away and expects to be asked. Please don't leave this until Thursday.

Press calls: two journalists asked for a call before the event, one from a trade newsletter and one from a Belgian daily. Hanna told them I would be available on Wednesday afternoon. The calendar has 14:00 and 15:00 slots, 20 minutes each, and Hanna still needs to confirm them. I won't be able to take them. Ask Hanna whether she wants to sit in with you or whether Geert should take them. Use 1.4 and not 2.1. If anyone asks about the error, say it was my mistake, that the corrected figure is in v7, and that the conclusion holds.

4. Thursday 26 November

The run of show in this folder is the old timing. Tomás's email from Monday asks for these changes: the presentation should be 15 minutes instead of 20, the panel should start at 12:50 instead of 12:55, and the MEP has a vote and must leave at 13:30. She wants to take at least two questions herself before she goes. That means Q&A has to come before 13:30, not at 13:40. Please confirm the final timing with Tomás on Wednesday and send him the final version.

Guests should be at the security entrance by 12:00. Lunch is served outside the room from 12:00. The embargo lifts at 10:00 CET, so the corrected release should already be out before then, and the old version should not be live anywhere.

Abena Owusu-Mensah joins remotely from Accra. The link is in the calendar invite, and you tested it on 18 November. Accra is an hour behind us, so at 12:50 CET it will be 11:50 there. Please check the link at about 12:30.

Lucy Tran from the Halvorsen Foundation is attending with a colleague.

5. The panel, and Florian Kessler

Florian Kessler (AESU) will raise two things. The first is the 80% pass-through assumption in section 4, which he says is much lower for small manufacturers. The second is resource shuffling, which he says we underestimate. His written comments are in this folder, dated 12 November.

Don't get defensive, and don't let him set the tone. The 80% is our central case. Annex B tests 40% and 60%. The result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%. Say that openly. On resource shuffling, section 5.2 already says it is a risk, and we recommend the Commission's monitoring report. Abena will probably back us on the LDC side. Lead with what the paper says about the LDCs, not with the methodology.

6. After Thursday

Lucy Tran needs two photos from the event and the attendance numbers for the Halvorsen grant report by 4 December. Ask the office or Hanna to take the photos, and count attendance from the security list.

7. Reaching me

You can call me. I'll be reachable until about 9 tomorrow morning. After 9 I might not pick up, so text me and I'll reply when I can. Geert knows I'm away and can make decisions you can't make alone.

I'm sorry for all of this, and I'm grateful for everything you've done on this paper. Thank you, Inês.

Marieke
